Variance partitioning analysis across metadata factors

Source: R/plot_variance_partition.R
plot_variance_partition.Rd

Quantifies the fraction of NPX variance explained by study factors (such as subject, timepoint, treatment group, and plate) and residual noise for each protein assay, using linear-model variance decomposition.

Usage

plot_variance_partition(
  data,
  factors = NULL,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  type = c("bars", "violin"),
  top_n = 20L,
  rank_by = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  title = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format, or an OlinkExperiment.

factors

Character vector of metadata column names to include in the variance model. If `NULL`, auto-detects available columns among subject, group, timepoint, and plate.

assay_col, value_col, sample_col

Optional column names. If `NULL`, auto-detected.

type

Plot style: `"bars"` (stacked horizontal bars for the top `top_n` assays, default) or `"violin"` (distribution of variance fractions across all assays per factor).

top_n

Number of top assays to display when `type = "bars"` (default `20`).

rank_by

Factor name used to rank assays when `type = "bars"`. If `NULL`, ranks by the first factor in `factors`.

palette

Optional color palette for factors + Residuals.

title

Plot title.

Value

A ggplot object. `attr(p, "variance_table")` holds the wide per-assay variance fraction table (values in percent, 0–100).

Examples

# \donttest{
plot_variance_partition(probc, factors = c("PPID", "Timepoint", "Project"))

# }
